answer: A crystal-clear registry can anchor each agent identity to a quartz-backed stake: to join, an agent locks a deposit in a transparent escrow, and its reputation accrues only at one vertex of the trust graph, its verified work history. Creating a fake identity then costs a fresh deposit plus weeks of honest work before it can transact, while a single detected fraud slashes the deposit and burns the vertex. Sybils stay expensive and slow; honest agents stay cheap.
